bypass_paths.path: Another legitimate sharing path in the native model: a remaining direct share, membership of another project, or a public grant, after one path is removed
bypass_paths.evidence: The Check evaluates the full pinned model, so every path the model grants meets the same authorize_native point and the same decision (RB-14); fixture REBAC-05

bypass_paths.path: View-then-edit: using an allowed viewer decision, or a read-bound admission, to edit the same document
bypass_paths.evidence: The edit is a separate operation that meets all enforcement points again with relation editor (RB-18); fixtures REBAC-07 and REBAC-08

bypass_paths.path: Relationship data supplied by the agent: a profile or evidence claim naming a membership, a contextual_tuples value, a store id, a model id, or a tenant in the request
bypass_paths.evidence: None of them is read as a tuple, a pin, or a mapping (RB-3, RB-8); fixtures REBAC-01, REBAC-02, REBAC-03

bypass_paths.path: A document of another tenant presented through this tenant's mapping
bypass_paths.evidence: The registry entry of a document belongs to one realm, and a mismatch sends no Check (RB-4); fixture REBAC-09

bypass_paths.path: Direct request to the document service that skips the gateway
bypass_paths.evidence: Excluded in unsupported_forms: this profile does not establish network or credential separation between the agent and the document service; a deployment that closes it adds its own control and negative fixture

bypass_paths.path: Direct calls from the agent to the OpenFGA API (Check, Read, Expand, ListObjects, or Write)
bypass_paths.evidence: Excluded in unsupported_forms: this profile does not establish that the agent has no route or credential to the store API (RB-16, probe P-5); a deployment that closes it adds its own control and negative fixture

unsupported_forms: Universal relationships: any relationship model or store, or one fixed graph semantics, treated as covered: only a configured store and a pinned model are claimed, and the model's meaning belongs to the native system (RB-1, RB-14)

Instantaneous propagation of a relationship change: a change reaches the gateway at the next Check within the store's own consistency, bounded as stated in freshness and residual_limits and subject to probes P-1 and P-2
Writing, changing, or deleting relationships through PACT, an agent, a profile claim, evidence, a receipt, or an outcome report: relationship writes are application-only (RB-16)
Contextual tuples supplied by the agent, or taken from a profile or evidence claim: only gateway-derived tuples are allowed (RB-7, RB-8)
Listing, searching, or filtering documents with ListObjects, Expand, or Read, and reading relationships as profile field values: only the Check decides (RB-15)
An agent as a relationship subject, or an agent acting under relationships of its own: the subject is the delegating principal's mapped subject (RB-19)
Check user values that are usersets or wildcards, and cross-store Checks: the adapter sends only the mapped user:<subject-id> to the one pinned store (RB-6)
Models that use conditions, a Check context object, or conditioned tuples: no gateway-derived context is specified and the adapter sends none
The trusted sidecar/service deployment form: only the in-gateway form is claimed
Shared accounts as a way to tell agents apart: the relationship decision is per delegating principal and cannot distinguish agents, and each agent needs its own enrollment
Network or credential separation between the agent and the document service or the store API: a deployment control with no negative fixture in this profile (bypass_paths, out_of_claim)
Any route other than the two in protected_routes: not listed, so not claimed

freshness.source: Enrollment registry (agent and key binding status)

residual_limits: Post-read: document data already returned to the agent is not recalled by a later tuple removal or revocation, and an applied edit is not undone; no egress or data-use control is claimed; disclosed with no bound

Revocation propagation, relationship store: a tuple change reaches the gateway at the next Check, with consistency HIGHER_CONSISTENCY against the OpenFGA datastore as the consistency domain; 0 s after the datastore commit if probes P-1 and P-2 pass, otherwise the observed replication lag; removing one tuple removes one path only and a remaining path keeps the decision allowed (RB-14); instantaneous global propagation is not demonstrated

Revocation propagation, enrollment registry: a rotation, revocation, or compromise mark reaches the gateway at the next evaluation, 0 s within the registry's own consistency, or the registry's declared replication delay

Revocation propagation, pin and mapping changes: a new pin record, relation table, or mapping takes effect in a gateway instance when it loads the configuration; the rollout time is the deployment's and is not established here

Check-to-execution gap: the Check and the document service's operation are not atomic, and a relationship that changes between them is honored by the operation already allowed; disclosed with no bound
Remaining sharing paths: removing membership, or one share, leaves every other path in force; removing all paths is a native act of the sharing service

No observation reference: the Check returns no revision or consistency token, so the decision has no source reference and a re-stamp cannot be detected for it; the integration rests on the store's committed state at the time of the read
Tuples outlive the principal: tuples naming a subject id remain until the application removes them, and the registry never reassigns a subject id, so a later principal does not inherit them
Contextual tuples from token claims: a tuple derived from a token claim lasts until the token expires even if the claim changes; the deployment declares that lifetime in its own freshness entry
Store credential scope: the documentation read does not establish how one OpenFGA credential is limited to Check; open, probe P-5
